_note: P9: the 7 check_silk TP waivers were PRUNED - they now match nothing. The silk rings they covered were DELETED at P9 to clear a separate, real dfm finding, so the findings no longer exist. A waiver that matches nothing is misleading. Remaining: 2 check_pdn waivers, still live. Kept for the record: the original check_silk finding WAS a checker defect (check_silk.py:172 buffers an unfilled circle into a filled disc), and the dfm finding on the SAME ring was a SECOND, different tool defect (lib/gerblib.py chords drawn arcs, collapsing a circle onto its own diameter). Two checkers flagging one innocent feature for two unrelated reasons is not corroboration - each had to be diagnosed separately.

waivers.reason: check_pdn waiver - CORRECTED REASON after the P8 fresh-context review. My original reasoning (a 'category error' about IC pins) was wrong about the mechanism. check_pdn never looks at the board at all: it filters decoupling.json associations by rail and errors when the list is empty. So the finding is a TRUE statement - no association names this rail, therefore no PDN check ever examined it. The waiver still stands, because the rail is genuinely covered elsewhere and nothing is hidden: the +5V bank physically exists (C10-C15, one 198.93 mm2 island, parity clean) and its adequacy is set by the LOAD STEP, verified analytically at P4 and disclosed at-limit in erc-waivers.md W2; GND integrity is enforced by check_current pour-neck errors at the full 3.3 A budget, which found and fixed real defects this phase. Quantitative coverage for both comes from check_irdrop on the real copper: +5V worst drop 8.96 mV, GND 1.1 mV. Waived HERE rather than via constraints pdn=false, because that flag would ALSO exclude both nets from check_irdrop. This entry covers +5V.
